narrative.overview: Public frontend for SheoJol: a shelter/basecamp community map for ride-hailing (ojol) drivers in Tangerang, rendered as a single coherent world — Dual-Theme Utility Neobrutalism. One visual system, two palettes (light and dark) driven by next-themes, defaulting to the system preference. The theme is a lamp, not a separate design: same categorical accents, same 1px/2px border language, same hard offset shadows in both palettes. The system is loud, print-plain, and tactile: bold border-heavy cards, utilitarian type, dot-level legend for the map, hard offset shadows that read as physical blocks. It deliberately avoids glassmorphism, gradient scrims, soft glow, and decorative ornament — every pixel earns placement.
keyCharacteristics: Driver-first utility: every surface answers "where do I safely stop right now?" in under 2 seconds; navigation is one tap away, always on-screen.
Honest density: informational surfaces are dense but legible; the map owns any viewport it shares.
One authored motion moment (scroll reveal); everything else is a tactile echo of the offset-shadow language.
Live data honesty: real counts, explicit skeleton/error states, and an honest LIVE vs DEMO flag.

rules.name: The One-Accent Rule
rules.body: A single primary accent per surface. Chips, KPIs, and FABs may be colorful (they encode categories), but no screen carries two competing primary actions.

rules.name: The Hard-Only Rule
rules.body: Elevation is either a flat surface or a hard offset shadow. No blur, no diffuse drop shadows, no gradient scrims anywhere — with one deliberate exception: the dashboard/landing header logo card is a frosted chip (bg-white/85 / dark:bg-slate-950/80 + backdrop-blur-md, rounded-2xl) so the live map reads through behind the brand mark. It is the only blur in the system.

rules.name: The Set-Register Rule
rules.body: Big numbers and headlines are always black (900) and tight-tracked; body weight never exceeds 600. If it isn't a number or a label, it isn't black.

rules.name: The Outline-Follows-Corner Rule
rules.body: When a 2px border meets a rounded corner, the border curves with the corner (bottom sheet top cap, modal), rather than stopping square. Consistency across every sheet is the point.

dos: Do use semantic tokens (bg, surface, edge, content, primary, accent) for all UI; hardcoded zinc/slate/emerald/cyan is forbidden except the documented deliberate exceptions.
Do keep interactive emphasis at 2px borders with hard offset shadows; pressed state translates down and collapses the shadow.
Do keep the near-black-on-bright-fill pair (zinc-950 on emerald/cyan/red/amber) in both palettes — it is the signature, measured AA.
Do theme all browser chrome (selection, scrollbars, popups, attribution, color-scheme) with the active palette.
Do show explicit skeleton rails, flat error/empty callouts, and a LIVE vs DEMO honesty flag; never fabricate counts.
Do keep one authored motion moment (scroll reveal) and honor prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't add backdrop blur, gradient scrims, glass panels, or any soft/shadow-glow elevation — depth is hard offset only (exception: the single frosted logo card in the map header, see The Hard-Only Rule).
Don't introduce a second font, a third green, or a separate "admin dark" palette; one world, two lamps.
Don't put a theme capsule in the dashboard top bar (the map control stack owns that switch on the map surface).
Don't add the bottom nav to the map surface — the map owns the viewport; BottomNav is lg:hidden on /me and /account only.
Don't write comments in source or conversational copy in the UI (e.g. no "Loading... please wait" prose; use skeleton rails instead).

Don't use emoji as chrome icons; one stroke-SVG family, with emoji surviving only on the pinned amenity tiles, the mobile account gear chip, and the account quick-action menu rows (wayfinding affordances, lg:hidden).
